steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Linear structure: events unfold chronologically — easy to follow, naturalistic tradition.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Non-linear structure: fragmented timeline — creates mystery, reflects psychological states, modernist technique.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cyclical structure: ends where it began — suggests inevitability, futility, or the impossibility of change.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tragedy: protagonist with fatal flaw (hamartia) leading to downfall (catharsis for audience).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between linear and non-linear dramatic structure, giving an example of each. | How does a cyclical structure affect the audience's understanding of a play's themes? | Compare tragedy and comedy as dramatic genres. How do they use different techniques to engage the audience?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Linear: events in time order (e.g. An Inspector Calls has a linear investigation). Non-linear: out of time order (e.g. Blood Brothers uses flashforward opening). steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the structure/genre precisely with its technical term Link structure to EFFECT on the audience — don't just describe it Know the Greek origins of tragedy terminology (hamartia, catharsis) Use specific play examples to illustrate each structure and genre
